items.informal_description:
A real number $ x $ is called a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if there exists a positive constant $ C $ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $ n $, there exists an integer $ m $ where $ x 
eq  rac{m}{n} $ and the absolute difference $ |x -  rac{m}{n}| $ is less than $  rac{C}{n^p} $.

items.informal_name: Legendre's Condition for Continued Fraction Convergents
items.informal_description: For a real number $\xi$ and integers $u, v$, the proposition states that $u$ and $v$ are coprime, if $v = 1$ then $\xi - u > -\frac{1}{2}$, and the absolute difference $|\xi - \frac{u}{v}|$ is strictly less than $\frac{1}{v(2v - 1)}$.
A real number $ x $ is called a Liouville number if, for every natural number $ n $, there exist integers $ a $ and $ b $ with $ b > 1 $ such that $ 0 < |x - \frac{a}{b}| < \frac{1}{b^n} $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Rational Approximation with Bounded Denominator and Error Bound
items.informal_description: For any real number $\xi$ and positive integer $n$, there exists a rational number $q$ with denominator $\leq n$ such that $|\xi - q| \leq \frac{1}{(n + 1) \cdot \text{den}(q)}$.

items.informal_name: Finiteness of Rational Approximations with Denominator Squared Bound
items.informal_description: For any rational number $\xi$, the set of rational numbers $q$ satisfying $|\xi - q| < 1/\mathrm{den}(q)^2$ is finite, where $\mathrm{den}(q)$ denotes the denominator of $q$ in lowest terms.

A real number $ x $ satisfies the Liouville condition with exponent $ 1 $, meaning there exists a positive constant $ C $ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $ n $, there exists an integer $ m $ with $ x \neq \frac{m}{n} $ and $ \left|x - \frac{m}{n}\right| < \frac{C}{n} $.
